summary: Set up nginx on node1 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 using certificates issued by a local CA and short-lived by design (5 min validity) so renewal is observable. A systemd timer (cert-renew.timer, every 30s) runs /usr/local/sbin/cert-renew.sh, which uses openssl x509 -checkend to detect certs within 180s of expiry, reissues via openssl ca, atomically replaces the fullchain, and runs `nginx -s reload` (graceful, connection-preserving). Verified two live automatic renewals occurred (serial 1000->1001->1002) while continuous curl polling against https://$NODE_IP:8443/ returned HTTP 200 with zero failures throughout, including the exact second of the cert swap. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, rebooted node1 via `reboot`, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified nginx, cert-renew.timer, the on-disk cert/CA state, and HTTPS all recovered post-reboot with no data loss (timer and nginx both enabled, survived reboot, resumed on schedule).
actions_performed: Built a local openssl CA under /etc/certmgr/ca and issued a 5-minute-lived server certificate
Configured nginx site listening on 8443 SSL with ssl_certificate/ssl_certificate_key pointing at /etc/certmgr/certs/fullchain.pem and server.key
Wrote /usr/local/sbin/cert-renew.sh: checks expiry with openssl x509 -checkend, reissues via openssl ca with atomic file replace, reloads nginx gracefully
Created and enabled cert-renew.service + cert-renew.timer (systemd, OnUnitActiveSec=30s) for automatic renewal

Verified initial HTTPS response (200) and two live automatic renewal cycles (serial 1000->1001->1002) via a foreground polling loop capturing per-second HTTP status and TLS cert serial, confirming zero downtime through the reload
Captured pre-reboot boot_id and service/cert/health baseline
Rebooted node1 via `reboot`, polled until exec responded, confirmed boot_id changed
Verified post-reboot recovery of nginx, cert-renew.timer, on-disk cert/CA state, and HTTPS 200 response

evidence.requirement: HTTPS served on port 8443 on node1
evidence.summary: nginx configured and started with 8443 ssl site; initial curl -sk https://$NODE_IP:8443/ returned http_code=200

cert-renew.timer (systemd, 30s interval) enabled and active; /var/log/cert-renew.log shows autonomous renewals at 13:10:36 (serial 1000->1001) and 13:12:40 (serial 1001->1002), each triggered by the checkend<180s threshold before the prior cert's notAfter, with no manual intervention

evidence.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests
evidence.summary: Foreground polling loop sampled https://$NODE_IP:8443/ every ~1s from 13:12:02 to 13:13:40, all http_code=200 with 0 FAIL entries; the TLS-served certificate serial visibly transitioned from 1001 to 1002 at 13:12:41, immediately after the 13:12:40 renewal log entry, with no failed request across the transition
Captured boot_id fa1e87e6-00f3-42d2-acc5-ad1df6c3d16a, nginx active, cert-renew.timer active with next-fire schedule, cert serial=1002/notAfter 13:17:40, and HTTPS 200 as the pre-restart baseline

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: reboot acknowledged and boot identity changed
evidence.summary: Issued `reboot` via nohup so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect; polled node1 until exec responded again and found boot_id changed to 6010ec36-1610-40f0-a4b4-62fad07b015c (new boot) with uptime -s showing a fresh boot time

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: post-restart recovery verified
evidence.summary: After reboot, nginx and cert-renew.timer both report active (auto-started via systemctl enable), on-disk cert state persisted (serial=1002, same notAfter as before reboot), and https://$NODE_IP:8443/ again returns http_code=200 with body 'ok'
